---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API (slack.com/api) to post and reply to messages, read channel history, list channels and users, create and invite to channels, upload files, add and remove reactions, and search messages. Use when the user asks to send a Slack message or DM, read or monitor Slack conversations, manage Slack channels, upload files to Slack, or automate a Slack workspace through its API.
---

# Slack API

Automate a Slack workspace through the official Web API at `https://slack.com/api/<method>`.

## Authenticate

1. Obtain a token: bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`. Get it from the user or the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable.
2. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (the bundled client does this automatically).
3. The token must have the scopes required by each method (see [references/api.md](references/api.md)); otherwise Slack returns `missing_scope` plus the scope names in `needed`.

## Make API calls

Use the bundled client script for every call — it handles auth, encoding, error reporting, and rate limits:

```bash
SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_api.cjs <method> --key value ...
```

Token resolution: `--token` flag first, then `SLACK_TOKEN`.

## Common operations

| Task | Call |
| --- | --- |
| Post a message | `chat.postMessage --channel C123 --text "Hello" --mrkdwn true` |
| Reply in a thread | `chat.postMessage --channel C123 --thread_ts 1712345678.123456 --text "Reply"` |
| Update/delete a message | `chat.update` / `chat.delete` with `--channel` and `--ts` |
| List channels | `conversations.list --types public_channel,private_channel --limit 200` |
| Read history | `conversations.history --channel C123 --limit 50` |
| Read a thread | `conversations.replies --channel C123 --ts <parent ts>` |
| List users | `users.list --limit 200` |
| Find a user | `users.lookupByEmail --email user@example.com` |
| Create a channel | `conversations.create --name my-channel` |
| Invite users | `conversations.invite --channel C123 --users U1,U2` |
| Open a DM | `conversations.open --users U123` (returns the DM channel id) |
| Upload a file | `files.upload --filename report.txt --file ./report.txt --channels C123` |
| Add a reaction | `reactions.add --channel C123 --name white_check_mark --timestamp 1712345678.123456` |
| Search | `search.messages --query "quarterly report"` |

## Rules of thumb

- **Check `ok`:** Slack returns HTTP 200 with `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` for most failures. The client exits non-zero and prints the error.
- **Use IDs, not names:** most methods need channel/user IDs. Resolve names with `conversations.list` / `users.list` or `users.lookupByEmail`.
- **Message identity:** `chat.postMessage` returns `channel` and `ts`; use them for update/delete/reactions.
- **Paginate:** list/search methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it as `--cursor`, or add `--paginate [n]` to follow cursors automatically.
- **Respect rate limits:** on HTTP 429, wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry; the client reports this explicitly.
- **Private channels:** an app can only manage channels it has been added to; a workspace member must invite the app's bot into private channels.

## Reference

Read [references/api.md](references/api.md) when you need:
- a method not listed above, with its required scopes,
- scope details or token-type restrictions,
- message formatting (mrkdwn) or Block Kit basics,
- the common-error table.

## Client script

`scripts/slack_api.cjs` is a dependency-free wrapper (Node 18+):

- `--key value` pairs become form-encoded parameters; `--json '<json>'` sends a raw JSON body (for `blocks`, `attachments`);
- `--file <path>` sends multipart form data (for `files.upload`);
- `--paginate [n]` follows `next_cursor` (default 10 pages) and merges the first array field;
- `--raw` prints the full JSON response; otherwise output is summarized and truncated to stay context-friendly;
- run `node scripts/slack_api.cjs --help` for usage details.

# Slack Web API Reference

Companion reference for the `slack-api` skill. Read on demand when you need method details, scopes, formatting, or error guidance.

## Table of contents

1. [Tokens and scopes](#1-tokens-and-scopes)
2. [Request format](#2-request-format)
3. [Response format](#3-response-format)
4. [Pagination](#4-pagination)
5. [Rate limits](#5-rate-limits)
6. [Method catalog](#6-method-catalog)
7. [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#7-message-formatting-mrkdwn)
8. [Block Kit basics](#8-block-kit-basics)
9. [Common errors](#9-common-errors)
10. [Workflow snippets](#10-workflow-snippets)

## 1. Tokens and scopes

| Token type | Prefix | Typical scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bot token | `xoxb-` | `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `channels:manage`, `users:read`, `files:write`, `reactions:write`, `im:write` |
| User token | `xoxp-` | Same scope names, but act on the user's behalf |

Notes:
- `search.*` methods require a **user** token; bot tokens get `not_allowed_token_type`.
- `chat:write.customize` is only needed to override the bot's name/icon per message.
- When a token lacks a scope, Slack returns `missing_scope` with `needed` and `provided` fields. The bundled client prints `needed` automatically.
- Verify a token at any time with `auth.test` (no scope).

## 2. Request format

- `POST https://slack.com/api/<method>` with the token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Body: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (default) or `application/json`; `files.upload` uses `multipart/form-data`.
- Parameter names are snake_case (`thread_ts`, `post_at`, `link_names`).

## 3. Response format

- Success: HTTP 200 with `{"ok": true, ...}`.
- Failure: HTTP 200 with `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", "needed": "<scope>", "provided": "<scope>"}`.
- Rate limited: HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

## 4. Pagination

- List/search responses include `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
- Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page; an empty string means the end.
- `limit` controls page size (default 100; maximum varies by method, commonly 200–1000).
- The bundled client follows cursors automatically with `--paginate [n]`.

## 5. Rate limits

- Limits are per-method tiers (Tier 1 ≈ 1+ req/min ... Tier 4 ≈ 100+ req/min per workspace).
- On HTTP 429, respect the `Retry-After` header (seconds) before retrying.
- The bundled client exits with code 3 on 429 and prints `Retry-After`.

## 6. Method catalog

### Messaging

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | Post a message | channel, text, mrkdwn, thread_ts, blocks, link_names | `chat:write` |
| `chat.update` | Edit a message | channel, ts, text, blocks | `chat:write` |
| `chat.delete` | Delete a message | channel, ts | `chat:write` |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | Message visible to one user | channel, user, text | `chat:write` |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | Schedule a message | channel, text, post_at (unix time) | `chat:write` |

### Conversations (channels)

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conversations.list` | List channels | types (public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im), limit, cursor, exclude_archived | `channels:read` |
| `conversations.history` | Messages in a channel (newest first) | channel, limit, cursor, oldest, latest, inclusive | `channels:history` |
| `conversations.replies` | Messages in a thread | channel, ts | `channels:history` |
| `conversations.info` | Channel details | channel, include_num_members | `channels:read` |
| `conversations.members` | Channel members | channel, limit, cursor | `channels:read` |
| `conversations.create` | Create a channel | name, is_private | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.invite` | Invite users | channel, users (comma-separated) | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.rename` | Rename a channel | channel, name | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | Archive / restore | channel | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.setTopic` / `setPurpose` | Set topic / purpose | channel, topic / purpose | `channels:manage` |
| `conversations.join` | Join a public channel | channel | `channels:write` |
| `conversations.leave` | Leave a channel | channel | `channels:write` |
| `conversations.open` | Open a DM / group DM | users (comma-separated), return_im | `im:write` (DM) / `mpim:write` (group) |
| `conversations.close` | Close a DM | channel | `im:write` |

### Users

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `users.list` | List workspace users | limit, cursor | `users:read` |
| `users.info` | User details | user | `users:read` |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Find a user by email | email | `users:read.email` |

### Files (v2)

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files.upload` | Upload a file | file (multipart) or content, filename, channel_id / channels, thread_ts | `files:write` |
| `files.info` | File details | file | `files:read` |
| `files.list` | List files | channel, limit, cursor, types | `files:read` |
| `files.delete` | Delete a file | file | `files:write` |

### Reactions

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reactions.add` | Add a reaction | channel, name (no colons), timestamp | `reactions:write` |
| `reactions.remove` | Remove a reaction | channel, name, timestamp | `reactions:write` |
| `reactions.get` | Get reactions on a message | channel, timestamp | `reactions:read` |

### Search (user tokens)

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search.messages` | Search messages | query, count, sort | `search:read` |
| `search.files` | Search files | query, count, sort | `search:read` |

### Pins and reminders

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pins.add` | Pin a message | channel, timestamp | `pins:write` |
| `pins.list` | List pins | channel | `pins:read` |
| `pins.remove` | Unpin a message | channel, timestamp | `pins:write` |
| `reminders.add` | Create a reminder | text, time (unix) | `reminders:write` |
| `reminders.list` | List reminders | — | `reminders:read` |

### Misc

| Method | Purpose | Key params | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `team.info` | Workspace info | — | — |
| `emoji.list` | Custom emoji | — | — |
| `auth.test` | Verify token | — | — |

## 7. Message formatting (mrkdwn)

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, ``` ``pre`` ```, `>quote`
- `<https://example.com|Link text>` — link with label
- `<@U123>` user mention, `<#C123>` channel link, `<!channel>` / `<!here>` / `<!everyone>` special mentions
- `:emoji:` emoji
- Pass `link_names: true` to auto-link `@name` and `#channel`
- Use `\n` for newlines in `text`; use blocks for rich layout

## 8. Block Kit basics

Send a `blocks` JSON array with `--json` (works with `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `files.upload`):

```json
{
  "channel": "C123",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Report ready" } },
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Summary:* 42 new signups" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    { "type": "actions", "elements": [ { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Open" }, "url": "https://example.com" } ] }
  ]
}
```

- Text objects use `{"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "..."}` or `{"type": "plain_text", "text": "..."}`.
- Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `header`, `actions`, `context`, `image`.

## 9. Common errors

| error | meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `not_authed` | No auth token |
| `invalid_auth` | Token invalid or revoked — request a new token |
| `account_inactive` | The user associated with the token is deactivated |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a scope; check the `needed` field |
| `not_allowed_token_type` | Wrong token type (e.g., bot token used with `search.*`) |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel id, or the bot is not in the channel |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived — unarchive first |
| `name_taken` | Channel name already exists |
| `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` malformed — use the exact `ts` returned by the API |
| `message_not_found` | Message deleted, or wrong `ts`/channel |
| `users_not_found` | User id(s) invalid |
| `already_in_channel` | User is already a member |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429 — retry after `Retry-After` seconds |
| `internal_error` | Transient — retry with backoff |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace admin policy blocks the action |

## 10. Workflow snippets

Resolve a channel name to an id:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list --types public_channel,private_channel --limit 200 --paginate
# match .name === "general" in the output, then use its id as --channel
```

Post a message, then act on it (thread reply, reaction, update):

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C123 --text "Deploy finished"
# note the returned ts, then:
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C123 --thread_ts <ts> --text "Details here"
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add --channel C123 --name white_check_mark --timestamp <ts>
```

Notes:
- `ts` format is `<unix seconds>.<microseconds>`, e.g. `1712345678.123456`; treat it as an opaque string.
- `conversations.history` returns messages newest-first; use `oldest`/`latest` (unix timestamps) to window.
- The app's bot must be a member of a private channel before it can read or post there.

## 7. Message formatting (mrkdwn)

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, ``` ``pre`` ```, `>quote`
- `<https://example.com|Link text>` — link with label
- `<@U123>` user mention, `<#C123>` channel link, `<!channel>` / `<!here>` / `<!everyone>` special mentions
- `:emoji:` emoji
- Pass `link_names: true` to auto-link `@name` and `#channel`
- Use `\n` for newlines in `text`; use blocks for rich layout

## 8. Block Kit basics

Send a `blocks` JSON array with `--json` (works with `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `files.upload`):

```json
{
  "channel": "C123",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Report ready" } },
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Summary:* 42 new signups" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    { "type": "actions", "elements": [ { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Open" }, "url": "https://example.com" } ] }
  ]
}
```

- Text objects use `{"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "..."}` or `{"type": "plain_text", "text": "..."}`.
- Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `header`, `actions`, `context`, `image`.

## 9. Common errors

| error | meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `not_authed` | No auth token |
| `invalid_auth` | Token invalid or revoked — request a new token |
| `account_inactive` | The user associated with the token is deactivated |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a scope; check the `needed` field |
| `not_allowed_token_type` | Wrong token type (e.g., bot token used with `search.*`) |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel id, or the bot is not in the channel |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived — unarchive first |
| `name_taken` | Channel name already exists |
| `invalid_timestamp` | `ts` malformed — use the exact `ts` returned by the API |
| `message_not_found` | Message deleted, or wrong `ts`/channel |
| `users_not_found` | User id(s) invalid |
| `already_in_channel` | User is already a member |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429 — retry after `Retry-After` seconds |
| `internal_error` | Transient — retry with backoff |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace admin policy blocks the action |

## 10. Workflow snippets

Resolve a channel name to an id:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list --types public_channel,private_channel --limit 200 --paginate
# match .name === "general" in the output, then use its id as --channel
```

Post a message, then act on it (thread reply, reaction, update):

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C123 --text "Deploy finished"
# note the returned ts, then:
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C123 --thread_ts <ts> --text "Details here"
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add --channel C123 --name white_check_mark --timestamp <ts>
```

Notes:
- `ts` format is `<unix seconds>.<microseconds>`, e.g. `1712345678.123456`; treat it as an opaque string.
- `conversations.history` returns messages newest-first; use `oldest`/`latest` (unix timestamps) to window.
- The app's bot must be a member of a private channel before it can read or post there.
